info.name: Petpooja — A Dough Cookie
info.description:
All nine Petpooja endpoints for **A Dough Cookie - Begur**.

## Two directions
- **Requests 1-4** — we call Petpooja (`{{pp_base}}`)
- **Requests 5-9** — Petpooja calls us (`{{our_base}}`). Sending these yourself simulates what their servers would do.

## Identity
| Id | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Menu-sharing code | `bw8dz5o93u` | **`restID` in every order relay** |
| Restaurant id | `449010` | A Dough Cookie - Begur, for their support |
| Sandbox row id | `5312` | dashboard only |
| Client id | `5147` | account level |

## Read this before trusting a green tick
**Petpooja returns HTTP 200 even when the call fails.** Success lives in the body, and `success` is the STRING `"1"`/`"0"` — except `rider_status_update`, which returns `"success"`. Checking the status code alone reports every failure as a success.

## Status (verified 2026-07-29)
✅ 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 — working
❌ 1 `save_order` — blocked on Petpooja activating the API service for restID 449010
⚰️ 4 `fetch menu` — deprecated by Petpooja

Full notes: `Petpooja_integration/PETPOOJA_API_REFERENCE.md`

request.description:
Cancels an order at the POS. **This is the only transition their API accepts** — `status` is always `-1`.

✅ Works. Returns `{"success":"1","message":"Order status updated successfully."}`

**Gotchas**
- Request field is `clientorderID`, response field is `clientOrderID` — different casing.
- Does NOT validate restID: a bogus code or an empty string still returns success:'1'.
- It DOES validate credentials — break one and you get `"Invalid client credentials." / GN_105`. That is the fastest way to prove the account is live (~400ms).

exec: // Petpooja returns HTTP 200 even on business failure — success lives in the BODY.

request.description:
Tells the POS the parcel moved, so the merchant sees delivery progress without polling. Maps onto Delhivery scan events.

`status`: `rider-assigned` | `rider-arrived` | `pickedup` | `delivered`

✅ Works. Returns `{"success":"success","message":"Your reuqest received succesfully"}`

⚠️ **`success` is the string `"success"` here, NOT `"1"`** as on every other endpoint. Code that checks `success === '1'` will treat every successful call as a failure.

item.name: B — Petpooja calls us
5. Push Menu — they send us the catalogue

request.description:
**Petpooja calls this on US.** They send the entire catalogue — a real one is 250-300 KB.

✅ Our side works: their 288 KB demo menu ingested in 3.2s (253 rows).
❌ **They have never actually called it.** Their trigger reports `request:[]`, `response:[]` — the outbound call is never constructed.

**Parsing traps**
- `in_stock: "2"` means **AVAILABLE**, not out of stock. Reading it the other way marks the whole catalogue unavailable and empties the storefront.
- Key on `details.menusharingcode`, NOT `restaurantid` — orders are relayed with the sharing code.
- `item_tax` is a comma-separated STRING here, but an ARRAY OF OBJECTS in an order.

This sample includes a variation item so you can see the expansion: 2 items in → 3 rows stored.

exec: // Petpooja returns HTTP 200 even on business failure — success lives in the BODY.

request.description:
**Petpooja calls this on US** when the merchant accepts, rejects or progresses an order. `callback_url` is sent per-order in Save Order — there is no dashboard field for it.

`orderID` is OUR order_number, echoed back.

| status | meaning | we set |
|---|---|---|
| -1 | Cancelled | CANCELLED |
| 1, 2, 3 | Accepted | CONFIRMED |
| 4 | Dispatched | OUT_FOR_DELIVERY |
| 5 | Food ready | PREPARING |
| 10 | Delivered | DELIVERED |

⚠️ This **really changes the order** in the database. `{{test_order_number}}` points at a test order. A DELIVERED/CANCELLED order is never walked backwards by a late or duplicate callback. An unknown order id answers HTTP 200 with success:'0' — a retry cannot fix a bad id.

exec: // Petpooja returns HTTP 200 even on business failure — success lives in the BODY.

item.name: 7. Item / Addon Stock — sold out or back

request.description:
**Petpooja calls this on US** when an item goes out of stock or comes back.

**One endpoint for both on and off** — set it as BOTH "Item Off API Endpoint" and "Item On API Endpoint" in their Configuration screen, as their docs advise.

`type` is `item` or `addon`. Set `inStock` to `false` to mark sold out.

Also mirrors onto `products.is_available`, so an item marked sold-out at the POS stops being orderable on our storefront — verified: flipping this really does flip the product.

exec: // Petpooja returns HTTP 200 even on business failure — success lives in the BODY.

item.name: 8. Get Store Status — are we open?

request.description:
**Petpooja calls this on US** to ask whether we are accepting orders.

`store_status` `1` = open, `0` = closed. An unknown store defaults to **open**, so a missing row can never silently block sales.

⚠️ Note the direction: there is **no** endpoint for asking Petpooja whether a store is open. Store status flows POS → us only.

exec: // Petpooja returns HTTP 200 even on business failure — success lives in the BODY.

request.description:
**Petpooja calls this on US** to open or close the store.

Set `store_status` to `"0"` to close, with an optional `reason` and `turn_on_time`. Send `"1"` to reopen.

Verified: closing then reopening persists in the database, not merely echoed back.
